name: Melbourne
title: Ultrasonic Gauging for Ships in Melbourne | Port Phillip UTM
description: UTM for ships at the Port of Melbourne: car carriers, Bass Strait ro-ro, container ships and tankers gauged alongside or at anchor, decks, ramps and tanks.
h1: Ship Thickness Gauging at the Port of Melbourne and Port Phillip
intro: Melbourne is Australia's busiest container port and its main gateway for imported vehicles, and tankers, Bass Strait freight ro-ro ships and cruise ships add to the traffic that enters through the narrow mouth of Port Phillip. The long passage up the bay is navigation time, so the gauging opportunity is the stay alongside at Swanson Dock, Webb Dock or the fuel berths, or a period at a bay anchorage. Technicians travel from India to the ship for every job; nobody from Atlantis is based in Victoria.

highlights.p: Pure car and truck carriers discharge large numbers of vehicles at Webb Dock's automotive terminals. Their ramps, hoistable decks, lashing points and the ballast tanks below wear in ways that general gauging scopes often miss, and the stay alongside gives time to measure them while discharge carries on.

The freight ro-ro ships running between Melbourne and Tasmania call on a fixed timetable. A gauging programme can be split across successive calls, covering one group of tanks or one vehicle deck each time, so the owner builds a complete condition record without taking the ship out of service.

highlights.h: Fuel tankers at the liquid berths
highlights.p: Melbourne takes refined fuel by sea through the tanker berths at Holden Dock and Gellibrand Pier. Product tankers on regular Asian runs can have ballast tanks, deck structure and cargo piping measured while they discharge, within the terminal's permit system and hot-work rules.

port.h: Through the Rip and up Port Phillip to Melbourne's docks
p: Every ship bound for Melbourne enters Port Phillip through the Heads, a narrow entrance between Point Lonsdale and Point Nepean where strong tidal streams meet the Bass Strait swell; the passage, known as the Rip, is timed to the tide and is one of the more demanding pilotage passages in Australia. Pilots from Port Phillip Sea Pilots board outside the Heads, and the ship then follows dredged channels across the bay to the mouth of the Yarra River and the docks around it. Ports Victoria manages navigation and the harbour master's functions in the bay, while the Port of Melbourne operates the land and berths under a long-term lease from the state. Ships that cannot berth on arrival anchor at designated anchorages inside the bay.

Containers dominate. Swanson Dock, just inside the river mouth, holds the long-established container terminals, and Webb Dock, on the bay side, adds a newer automated container terminal next to its automotive berths. Appleton Dock and the river berths take break-bulk, project cargo and dry bulk, while the liquid berths serve the fuel and chemical storage at Coode Island and Yarraville. Station Pier at Port Melbourne is the cruise terminal, busiest in the southern summer. The Spirit of Tasmania passenger ferries moved their base to Geelong in 2022, but freight ro-ro ships to and from Tasmania still sail from Melbourne, and coastal traffic, feeder ships and deep-sea container services from Asia, Europe and the Pacific make up the rest.

A ship can spend many hours inside port limits between the Heads and its berth, but none of that is inspection time. What matters for gauging is the stay alongside, from about a day for a container ship to longer for a heavy-lift or project cargo call, and any period at a bay anchorage while the ship waits for a berth or for orders. Winter brings strong westerly and south-westerly weather into Bass Strait, which can stop pilot boarding at the Heads for periods and stretch schedules; summer adds cruise congestion at Station Pier. The docks lie in the shelter of Hobsons Bay and the lower Yarra, so once a ship is alongside, weather rarely stops work in its tanks.

facilities.h: Berths, anchorages and docking options for ships at Melbourne
p: Gauging at Melbourne is done alongside or at anchor. At the container and automotive terminals the team works around stevedoring and keeps out of crane and vehicle lanes; at the fuel berths, the terminal's safety rules decide which tanks and pipelines can be opened during discharge, and any cargo tank entry needs a gas-free certificate. A ship at a bay anchorage is reached by a launch booked through the agent, and the relative shelter of Port Phillip makes this more practical than at most open-coast Australian ports. Anyone without a Maritime Security Identification Card is escorted inside port security zones, so the agent arranges an escort from the terminal gate.

Melbourne has no commercial drydock that takes ocean-going merchant ships. The historic graving dock at Williamstown is not a commercial repair dock for merchant ships, and smaller slipways around the port handle tugs, pilot boats, dredgers and workboats. Merchant ships trading to Melbourne dock in Asia, so readings taken during a Melbourne call usually become the basis of the yard's steel specification. Bass Strait ro-ro ships, with their fixed timetables, are often gauged in stages across several calls instead.
list: Swanson Dock container terminals — deck plating, hatch coamings and scrubber discharge piping measured during cargo work.
Webb Dock automotive and container berths — car carrier ramps, hoistable decks and ballast tanks; container ship deck structure.
Holden Dock and Gellibrand Pier — product tankers discharging fuel; ballast tanks, deck and cargo piping under terminal rules.
Appleton Dock and the river berths — break-bulk, project cargo and dry bulk ships alongside for discharge.
Port Phillip anchorages — owner's condition and pre-purchase gauging on ships waiting for a berth, boarded by launch.
Station Pier — cruise ships on turnaround; scrubber and void space pipework.

context.h: Victoria's port authorities, AMSA and seasonal biosecurity
p: AMSA carries out port state control in Victoria as elsewhere in Australia, which is a member of both the Tokyo MoU and the Indian Ocean MoU. On vehicle carriers and ro-ro ships, a large share of Melbourne's traffic, an inspection naturally takes in ramps, watertight and weathertight doors and vehicle-deck fittings as well as hull structure, and wastage at ramp hinges or deck sockets is the kind of finding owners prefer to discover themselves first. Ports Victoria's harbour master sets the rules for ships in the bay, including the conditions for anchoring and for transiting the Heads, and the agent confirms them before any work at anchor is planned.

Biosecurity matters even more in the vehicle trade. Besides the biofouling reporting every international arrival has made since 15 June 2022, the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry applies seasonal measures against the brown marmorated stink bug, roughly from September to April, aimed at vehicles, machinery and the ships that carry them. Ro-ro ships and car carriers from target countries may be inspected or have cargo treated, which can change berthing times, so owners planning gauging during a car carrier's Melbourne call should leave some slack in the schedule. Ballast water must also be managed to Australian requirements, and fitting a treatment system is a common reason to check the condition of ballast tanks and piping.

psc: Tokyo MoU and Indian Ocean MoU

jobs.h: Typical thickness measurement work at Melbourne
jobs.p: The Melbourne workload follows the port's trades. Car carriers and ro-ro ships bring structural questions about decks, ramps and the tanks beneath them; container ships need deck and coaming readings and scrubber piping checks; product tankers need ballast tank and piping condition for vetting and for the owner's planning. Because merchant ships are not docked here, most jobs are condition gauging between surveys, steel estimates ahead of an Asian docking, or pre-purchase inspections arranged while the ship is alongside. We fix the scope with the superintendent against the berth window or anchorage period, mobilise from India once visas and dates are confirmed, and issue readings on the class formats. On the Bass Strait ships, a programme can be spread over several calls to suit the timetable.
list: Hoistable deck, ramp and ballast tank gauging on a car carrier discharging at Webb Dock, with magnetic particle crack checks at the ramp hinges.
A staged condition gauging programme on a Bass Strait freight ro-ro ship, one vehicle deck and tank group per call.
Pre-docking steel estimate for a container ship at Swanson Dock before its renewal survey in Asia.
Cargo piping and ballast tank gauging on a product tanker at Holden Dock for the owner's vetting file.
Pre-purchase inspection of a break-bulk ship at Appleton Dock, covering holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks.

logistics: Melbourne Airport at Tullamarine is the usual arrival point, with road access to the docks around the Yarra mouth and to the Williamstown berths. Indian nationals need an Australian visa suitable for short specialist assignments, applied for as soon as dates firm up because processing times vary. The ship's agent arranges terminal entry and security escorts, confirms biosecurity clearance, and books a launch for any work at a Port Phillip anchorage.

faqs.q: Can a ship be gauged at anchor in Port Phillip?
faqs.a: Yes, and the bay's shelter makes it a reasonable option. A ship waiting for a berth or for orders at a designated anchorage can be boarded by launch, arranged by the agent within the harbour master's rules. Ballast tanks, voids, deck structure and piping can be measured; cargo tanks need gas-free certificates first. Strong winds across the bay can still stop launch transfers, so we keep the scope flexible and ranked.

faqs.q: Can a car carrier's decks be gauged while vehicles are being discharged?
faqs.a: Partly. Decks and ramps in active use are off-limits for safety, but decks already cleared can be measured as the stevedores work through the ship, and ballast tanks and voids below the vehicle decks are independent of the discharge. Planning the sequence with the chief officer and the stevedoring supervisor lets the team follow the discharge deck by deck.

faqs.q: Where do ships trading to Melbourne go for drydocking?
faqs.a: Usually to yards in Asia. Melbourne has no commercial drydock for ocean-going merchant ships, so the realistic approach is to gauge during a Melbourne call, ahead of the docking, and send the yard a measured steel estimate. That cuts the yard's discovery work at the start of the docking and gives the owner a firm basis for the repair specification.

faqs.q: Do stink bug inspections affect gauging plans?
faqs.a: They can. During the brown marmorated stink bug season, roughly September to April, ro-ro ships and vehicle carriers from target countries may be inspected or have cargo treated, which can shift berthing and discharge times. We schedule the gauging with a margin and keep the agent informed of the team's plans, so a change in the biosecurity programme does not waste the visit.
